To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) The resistivity of a pure Si NW is significantly higher than that of a Si/SiGe and a Ge NW, and that the Si/Si1-xGex NWs are more conductive than a pure Si NW.
the electrical properties of the Si/SixGe1-x NWs are significantly different from the pure Si NWs and the Ge NWs, which is attributed to the current conduction of the surface states.

the electrical properties of epitaxially grown single-crystallinity Si/SiGe nanowires are strongly influenced by the presence of surface states and the Si/Si1-xGex nanowire heterostructures are more influenced than the Si or Ge ones. In summary, our research is concerned with

the fabrication of single crystal semiconductor nanowires (Si, Si/SiGe and Ge) by molecular beam epitaxial growth and the electrical characterization of the nanowires by in-situ electrical measurements in an electron microscope.
the electrical characterization of Si/SiGe nanowires grown on silicon substrate by molecular beam epitaxial technique.
the growth, characterization and modeling of Si/SiGe nanowires.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the surface state conduction is the major current carrier in the NWs.
the surface states of the NWs, rather than the band diagram, are responsible for the electrical properties of the NWs.
the electrical properties of the Si/SGe heterostructure and pure Si/Ge NWs are not dominated by the carrier transport in the core of the NWs, but by the surface states.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Si NWs with compositionally graded segments of a few nanometer in thicknesses can be grown by molecular beam eptaxy, and the Si/Si1-xGex heterostructure NW is an interesting system for studying the electrical properties of NWs. the surface states play an important role in the electrical conduction of the epitaxially grown single-crystallline Si/SiGe/Si heterostructure NW and the electrical conduction is more strongly influenced in the Ge or SiGe NWs than in the Si NW.
the electrical properties of Si NWs are strongly influenced by surface states and the surface states can be controlled by the surface passivation and the surface composition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Si/Si1-xGex heterostructure NW grown by molecular beam deposition can be used for nanoelectronic device applications.
the electrical characteristics of NWs are strongly influenced by their surface states.

, in addition to the band structure and the surface states, the composition and the thickness of the graded Si1-x Gex segments in the Si/Si1-x Gex heterostructures play important roles in the electrical properties of the Si/S1-x Gex NWs.
